THE LETTER

INT. FAMILY HOME - KITCHEN - EARLY MORNING

A small kitchen. Steam rises from a pot. MEERA (58), practical, her hands never still, stirs lentils. She keeps glancing at the door.

RAVI (32) stands in the doorway in a BLUE JACKET, a travel bag on his shoulder. He has not slept. His younger sister ANU (19) watches from the table, chewing her nail.

MEERA
You are leaving today. You did not even tell me.

RAVI
I was going to tell you tonight, Ma.

MEERA
Tonight is too late for telling.

A knock. Ravi opens the door. A POSTMAN hands him a thick envelope. The name on it reads R. KUMAR. Ravi's face changes. He slips the LETTER into his jacket pocket before Meera can see it.

ANU
What was that?

RAVI
Nothing. Bills.

The elder son picks up his bag and leaves without eating.

EXT. DUSTY ROAD OUTSIDE THE VILLAGE - MORNING

Ravi walks fast, head down. UNCLE HARI (65), a retired schoolteacher on an old bicycle, stops beside him.

UNCLE HARI
Running away from breakfast, R. Kumar? Your mother will not forgive you.

RAVI
I need someone to read this. My eyes are tired.

He takes out the LETTER and hands it to Uncle Hari. The old man reads slowly, and his smile fades.

UNCLE HARI
This is the offer you wanted. The city job. And you were going to hide it?

RAVI
She will think I am abandoning her.

Uncle Hari folds the letter and keeps it in his shirt pocket. Ravi turns to go, stumbles on a loose stone and falls hard. He cuts his left palm on the gravel. Uncle Hari ties his handkerchief around the wound.

UNCLE HARI
Go home. Tell her yourself. A letter is only paper.

Ravi nods, unable to speak.

INT. FAMILY HOME - LIVING ROOM - EVENING

The light is low. Ravi sits on the floor, now in a RED CHECKED SHIRT, the handkerchief still tied around his palm. Meera sits across from him, silent. Anu brings tea and puts a cup in front of each of them.

MEERA
Your father also left once. For work. He came back thin and quiet.

RAVI
I will come back, Ma.

MEERA
Will you? Or will the city keep you?

Anu sits between them and takes both their hands. Nobody speaks. The tea goes cold.

INT/EXT. FAMILY HOME - COURTYARD - NIGHT

Crickets. A single lamp hangs from a nail. Meera sits alone on a cot. Ravi comes out and sits beside her. He is still in the red checked shirt.

RAVI
Uncle Hari read me the letter today. They want me in two weeks.

He pulls the LETTER from his pocket and places it in Meera's hands. She cannot read it. She holds it against her chest.

MEERA
Then read it to me. Slowly. I want to hear what my son is worth.

Ravi begins to read. Anu appears at the door and listens in the dark.
